proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 80, 5^n is congruent to 5^(n mod 6) modulo 7.

argument.text: At n = 0 both sides equal 1 modulo 7.
The residue 5 has order 6 modulo 7: for every n in [0, 74], 5^(n+6) is congruent to 5^n modulo 7.
Every integer n in [1, 80] is even or odd, so the two cases below are exhaustive.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 80].
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 80, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 6.
Every n in [0, 80] falls in exactly one residue class modulo 6.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 80: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 6.
For every n in [0, 80]: if 6 divides n then 5^n is congruent to 1 modulo 7.
There exists an integer n in [1, 80] with n^2 > 80.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 80 we have n^2 >= 2n.
Periodicity plus the base case gives the statement for every n in [0, 80].
